policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'bring back their captivity' does not distinguish the qere from the ketiv, and the mapped note is classed alternative_rendering, so it cannot decide the reading.
ASV explicitly renders the first-person possessive in 'the remnant of my nation,' distinguishing qere גּוֹיִ֖י ('my nation') from ketiv גוי ('nation').
